svg.title: Gateway Offloading
svg.desc: Gateway Offloading. Move TLS termination, authentication and compression out of every service into the gateway. Step 1, Plumbing in every service: Every service repeats the same plumbing in its own language, and one certificate is about to expire. Step 2, Move it to the gateway: The shared work moves into the gateway: one certificate, one auth configuration, one place to patch. Step 3, One request at the edge: The gateway ends TLS, answers a bad token with 401, forwards the identity, logs and compresses. Step 4, Know the limits: Business rules stay in the service, the hop behind the gateway is secured, the gateway is redundant.

g.text: Every service repeats the same plumbing in its own language, and one certificate is about to expire.
The shared work moves into the gateway: one certificate, one auth configuration, one place to patch.
The gateway ends TLS, answers a bad token with 401, forwards the identity, logs and compresses.
Business rules stay in the service, the hop behind the gateway is secured, the gateway is redundant.
The same plumbing in every service
three teams, each renews its own
One place to patch a vulnerability
only the gateway may connect, over TLS or mTLS
Behind the gateway: a call that bypasses it is refused
so it runs as several redundant instances
